clue.text: Green scientists record one amongst energy expenses

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: amongst places the record-and-one pair within the word for expenses

parts.note: expenses are costs
to log is to record
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Environmentally minded researchers keep a note of their spending on power.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecology is the green cause, and its scientific specialists study how living things interact with their environment.

clue.text: Refuse to turn up without signs of wear

parts.note: bran is husk, the waste of milled grain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for to turn is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: wend is an old verb meaning to turn or go

explanation.surface: Someone declines to show up wearing anything that is not pristine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses WEND to DNEW beneath BRAN; wend originally meant 'turn', as in wending one's way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely new and unused shows no marks of use or wear.

clue.text: Country series overlooked by reader

indicators.note: the series abbreviation is passed over, so it is dropped from the word for reader

parts.note: a peruser is someone who reads

explanation.surface: A run of books gets ignored by the person reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Sex symbol? Little point for boozers

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar
a dot is a small point

explanation.surface: A sly question about a tiny pub sign promising a glamour star.
explanation.walkthrough: Brigitte Bardot, the French actress, was a famous sex symbol of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: The French film star was the archetypal screen siren, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Italy supports nobleman ousting university director

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter sits underneath, so this letter goes last
ousting means the university letter is thrown out of the nobleman's title

parts.note: a viscount is a nobleman ranking below an earl
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An aristocrat props up Italy after a university head is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Luchino Visconti was an Italian film and stage director, himself from a noble family.
explanation.definitionFit: Luchino Visconti directed films such as The Leopard and Death in Venice.

clue.text: Extinct reptile's end with no raptor losing tail in struggle

indicators.note: a struggle throws things into disorder, so the letters are mixed up
the final letter of the word raptor is cut off

explanation.surface: A prehistoric creature meets its doom when no bird of prey is left fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' cuts RAPTOR to RAPTO; 'in struggle' rearranges END NO RAPTO.
explanation.definitionFit: This flying reptile of the Cretaceous period died out with the dinosaurs.

clue.text: Street transport on wheels? Go by foot

parts.note: to roll is to move along on wheels

explanation.surface: A question of whether to take wheeled transport down the street or walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk is a gentle journey made on one's feet.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge twenty-fifth hideout?

parts.note: a den is a hidden lair
Y is the twenty-fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone won't admit to a secret hiding place used on the twenty-fifth.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown or reject a claim is to decline to accept or admit it.

clue.text: Condemn treatment after son's brought in

indicators.note: the son's letter is brought into the word for treatment

parts.note: a cure is a medical treatment
S is the abbreviation for son; the apostrophe-s stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A doctor's remedy is damned once a boy is admitted to hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To damn someone or call down evil on them is to condemn them.

clue.text: American anger about sums handed over for philosopher

indicators.note: about means the word for anger wraps around the reversed sums

parts.note: to rile is to anger

indicators.note: handed over suggests turning the word for sums over, read backwards

parts.note: tots are sums added up

explanation.surface: A furious American passes on some calculations to a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handed over' is the reversal signal: the sums are turned over before going in. 'about' puts the anger word outside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker Aristotle, pupil of Plato, is one of the founders of Western philosophy.

clue.text: More than half lose strength, having recalled obscure writing and ancient tongue

indicators.note: only five of the eight letters of the word for losing strength are kept, so the end is dropped

parts.note: to languish is to weaken or lose vigour

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for obscure writing is read in reverse

parts.note: a code is writing made deliberately obscure

explanation.surface: A scholar weakens after revisiting a cryptic old text in a dead language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than half' keeps LANGU from LANGUISH; 'recalled' turns CODE into EDOC.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval Romance language of southern France, Occitan, used 'oc' for yes, giving its name.

clue.text: Spacious heavens seen behind Australian icon

indicators.note: the exclamation comes behind, so it follows the Australian animal

parts.note: the kangaroo, or roo, is a national symbol of Australia
'My!' and 'Heavens!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: The vast open sky stretches out behind a kangaroo emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with plenty of space is commodious and large.

clue.text: Report: "Turned cosy and warm"

indicators.note: turned means the word for cosy is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: snug means cosy
hot means very warm

explanation.surface: A quoted description of something that became comfortable and toasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, such as the crack of a fired weapon.

clue.text: Stink about one supporting working with gold getting a primarily ridiculous fee

indicators.note: the word for stink goes around everything else

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter goes beneath, so this letter follows the rest

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of ridiculous is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A smelly row over a gold-backed payment that seems absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a voluntary payment for professional services, often given to a speaker.

clue.text: Cause perplexity in new place located in a bit of common?

indicators.note: the new-and-place letters are set inside the word for common sense

parts.note: nous is common sense, so it is part of the phrase common sense
Pl. is the abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: A newly found spot sited on a village green baffles people.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS is common sense, so the question mark flags 'common' standing for only part of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone baffled or at a loss is to puzzle them.

clue.text: Well arranged, yet miscast, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A neatly organised production, though the actors may be in the wrong roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something methodical and orderly is done according to a plan.

clue.text: Swoons with two ladies, working to do this?

definitions.text: Swoons with two ladies, working to do this?

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A young man faints in the company of two women, and that's what youthful excess looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges SWOONS plus TWO LADIES; the whole clue describes youthful philandering.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to indulge in wild behaviour, especially romantic escapades, while young.

clue.text: Who has Spain included in distribution of rations?

definitions.text: Who has Spain included in distribution of rations?

indicators.note: the Spain letter is put among the letters of rations
distribution suggests the letters being handed out in a new order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A riddle about who joins in when Spain shares out food supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a young Spanish woman, who naturally includes Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A señorita is an unmarried Spanish woman, so she literally contains Spain.

clue.text: Disney perhaps picking up schedule with bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up means lifting the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties
the mina, or myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Walt Disney collects a timetable along with a feathered friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney made cartoons, so he is an example of someone who brings drawings to life.

clue.text: Colouring's s-slight, mostly

parts.note: the stammered S is taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for slight is dropped

parts.note: an affront is a slight or insult

explanation.surface: Someone stammers that a dye is mostly understated.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 's-' gives a lone S; the 's after Colouring is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron, from crocus stigmas, is used to tint food yellow-orange.

clue.text: Curious fellow retaining alien obsession

indicators.note: retaining means the strange fellow holds the alien inside

parts.note: an odd or queer fish is a strange person
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: An odd man keeps a space visitor as his strange fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation or compulsive devotion to something is an unhealthy preoccupation.

clue.text: Black tree caught in a particular blaze

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the tree is caught inside the words for a particular one

parts.note: one means a particular one, as in 'one day'
the fir is a conifer

explanation.surface: A dark tree goes up in a specific fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A large outdoor fire, such as on Guy Fawkes night, is a big blaze.

clue.text: Childlike error about old lady's rear

indicators.note: the word for error goes around the other pieces

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder or mistake

indicators.note: rear means the last letter of the word lady is taken

explanation.surface: A mistake concerning an elderly woman's backside seems juvenile.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British slang for a mistake; it surrounds O and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Childlike and youthfully immature describe someone like a young lad.

clue.text: Sommelier possibly not offering one non-alcoholic drink

indicators.note: not offering means the one is left out of the word for server

parts.note: a sommelier is a wine waiter, so an example of a waiter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wine expert refuses to pour anything but a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The plainest drink of all contains no spirits or wine whatsoever.

clue.text: One's ineffectual with mischievous child

parts.note: an imp is a naughty child

explanation.surface: Someone is hopeless when left with a naughty youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble, timid person is someone who is weak and ineffective.

clue.text: A glory when hybridised in the manner of an apple

indicators.note: hybridising crosses things, mixing the letters into a new form

parts.note: à la is French for in the manner of

explanation.surface: A splendid fruit tree is crossbred to produce a new apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a popular eating variety, a red-flushed sport of the Gala cultivar.

clue.text: Go East, moving forward in body of water

indicators.note: the East letter moves to an earlier place in the word for body of water

parts.note: a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Instructions to head east, sailing ahead across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: E moves forward from the end of LAKE to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a leak is slang for urinating, which is also to go to the toilet.

clue.text: Capital city beset by simple plant insects

indicators.note: the capital is surrounded by the plant word

parts.note: moss is a primitive non-flowering plant
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A city surrounded by basic vegetation swarming with bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: These biting flies spread malaria and are common pests.

clue.text: Excellent disposition of oil in dressing

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A first-rate arrangement of oil for a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: This garlic mayonnaise from Provence is a sauce or condiment.
